rationale: The assistant correctly latched onto the key evidence (new drawer unit, roaring fan, cuts out on high) and leaned toward overheat protection from restricted ventilation, with a sensible 'switch off and isolate the power first' before any checking. However, the turn-3 'quick test' merely reproduced the symptom the customer had already described and added no diagnostic value, and after the customer twice refused to look under the hob the final reply still asked them to 'ensure there is at least a few centimetres of space', never clearly handing off to the installer/fitter to check clearances or asking them to note the flashing code next time. The final heading listing 'pan misuse' contradicts the customer's confirmed induction pans, and an irrelevant 'suitable replacement' model-number panel appeared with no part in question. Useful direction reached but no concrete, actionable fix for a customer who asked 'so whats the fix?'.
